title: Rights come with responsibilities
examples: Why do rights come with responsibilities?
What are my responsibilities as a child?

right.label: Respect others
right.ask: What are my responsibilities as a child?

explain.say: Picture a seesaw in the park. If one side is much heavier, it crashes down and nobody has fun. A right is something you are free to have or do; a responsibility is something you should do. Look at the board: rights on the left, responsibilities on the right.

right.label: Respect others
right.ask: What are my responsibilities as a child?

explain.say: See the right to learn on the left? Nearly every country promises children an education; India made school free for every child aged 6 to 14 in 2009. Can you guess which responsibility balances it?

right.label: Respect others
right.ask: What are my responsibilities as a child?

explain.say: Yes, look across: do your best. Turn up, try hard, and let others learn too. Your right to learn sits with a duty not to stop anyone else learning. Can you see the seesaw level out?

right.label: Respect others
right.ask: What are my responsibilities as a child?

explain.say: Now free speech on the left: you may say what you think. It balances with respect for others: no bullying and no hurtful lies. Your freedom stops where it harms someone else. Can you think of an example?

right.label: Respect others
right.ask: What are my responsibilities as a child?

explain.say: See respect for others light up? Grown-up citizens add more duties, like obeying laws, paying taxes and voting. Brilliant balancing! Wow: India's constitution has 11 Fundamental Duties, including protecting nature and growing a scientific way of thinking.

right.label: Respect others
right.ask: What are my responsibilities as a child?

faq.a: A right is something every person should be free to have or do, like going to school, being safe or speaking your mind. Laws and agreements protect rights.
A responsibility is something you should do, for yourself or for others, like being kind, following fair rules and looking after shared things.
Yes. Most rights stop where they harm others. Free speech, for example, usually does not cover threats or lies that damage someone.

faq.q: What are my responsibilities as a child?
faq.a: Treat others kindly, look after shared things, follow fair rules, go to school and try your best, and speak up if someone is being hurt.

faq.q: What duties do adult citizens have?
faq.a: Obeying the law, paying taxes, and voting where it is allowed or required. Some countries also have jury duty or military service.
asks: What do citizens have to do?

facts: India's Right to Education Act (2009) gives every child aged 6 to 14 the right to free schooling.
India's constitution lists 11 Fundamental Duties in Article 51A.

quiz.say: Which responsibility goes with the right to free speech?
quiz.show: Which responsibility goes with the right to free speech?
quiz.why: You can speak freely, but you should not bully or spread hurtful lies.

wrong.0: Pocket money has nothing to do with free speech.
wrong.2: Watching TV is a choice, not a responsibility.

quiz.why: A responsibility is a duty, something you should do for yourself or others.

wrong.1: A gift is something you receive, not something you must do.
wrong.2: A holiday is a break, not a duty.
